archimedes-leaf-170.reason: Locating a privately held leaf depends on ownership correspondence that is mostly offline. The 1906 photo helps with identification but not with location. Finding it would recover one leaf of a key witness to Archimedes.

vermeer.reason: There is no document of optical aid use, and optical effects have competing explanations from image evidence alone. New public material is unlikely to settle the question.

zhou-conquest.reason: The dispute turns on calendar conventions and event identifications that existing evidence cannot adjudicate without new finds. A secure date would anchor early Chinese chronology.

wax-cylinder-voices.reason: Recordings can be matched with discographies, family papers and the press, and the Grant lead is concrete. Each identification is small, but a method would extend to many cylinders.

yamatai.reason: The itinerary is internally inconsistent, and archaeology lacks a naming inscription. A century of debate suggests document analysis cannot decide between Kyushu and Kinai.

eruption-1809.reason: The 1808/1818 citation conflict can probably be resolved from the Latin source. Identifying the actual volcano still needs physical tephra evidence the team cannot obtain.

oracle-bones.reason: Rare graphs and name-only signs resist decipherment. Computational analysis may read some, but a convincing reading of 'thousands' as posed is unlikely.

indus.reason: Very short inscriptions limit statistical tests, and earlier entropy studies stayed inconclusive. A decisive answer would reshape South Asian prehistory.

qing-literacy.reason: Contract signatures support estimates of signing ability for a selective population. Extending that to population-wide reading remains an inference problem.

americas-1492.reason: Post-contact sources and patchy archaeology leave estimates spanning an order of magnitude. Archival work alone will not close the range.

punt.reason: Provenance studies already point regionally, toward the Eritrea and Somali coasts. Transshipment through intermediate ports blocks precise location without new isotopic sampling.

cassini-cas-a.reason: The journals are online and the Cas A position is known, so the question is checkable. It depends on positional precision, and a negative answer may also be convincing. A result would refine the supernova's date.

ptolemy.reason: Statistical tests on errors, precession and latitude-dependent visibility are tractable and have advanced already. A checkable verdict on the mixed origin is plausible.

segmented-sleep.reason: Large-scale text mining with deduplication of quotations is well suited to an agent team. It can bound prevalence and its social distribution.

thylacine.reason: The extinction date depends on how unverifiable sightings are weighted. Archival work can sharpen the record but not resolve the probabilistic disagreement.

quran-standardization.reason: Dating requires lab and paleographic access, and coverage of variants is uneven. The question is contested and high-stakes, and synthesis alone is unlikely to settle it.

justinianic-plague.reason: The evidence is indirect, regionally fragmented and already intensely debated (maximalist vs minimalist). A convincing mortality figure is unlikely.

potato-blight-ships.reason: Port reports and newspapers allow linking some shipments to first outbreaks. Farm-level delivery links remain the weak point.

black-death-africa.reason: A convincing answer needs aDNA or burial evidence, which is beyond the team's reach. Texts are sparse, and abandonment of settlements has many possible causes.

silver-china.reason: Registered flows can be compiled, but smuggling and Japanese silver keep totals model-dependent. A better-bounded estimate is feasible, a convincing one less so.

linear-a.reason: Rigorous chance-baseline tests are feasible and could convincingly reject families. A positive identification is very unlikely, so the chance credits mostly negative results.

wilkinson-ciphers.reason: The code is dictionary-based, and the published key pairs plus edition comparison should permit decryption of accessible letters. Some originals are hard to reach. Decryption would document Wilkinson's treason.

russian-flu.reason: Age-specific mortality data exist and can be standardized. A checkable answer is likely, and it bears on epidemiological debates about the 1889 pathogen.

jupiter-red-spot.reason: Dated drawings plus computed central meridians can test continuity. Ambiguity in the marks may leave a qualified answer. A result matters for the Spot's longevity.

indian-ocean-tsunamis.reason: Searchable Ming records help, but Aceh coverage is thin and a negative result is hard to make convincing. A find would aid hazard history.

mughal-dodo.reason: Plausible routes via Surat are known, but tracing a specific bird needs a document that may not exist. The interest is mostly local.

agade.reason: Without excavation or a naming inscription, textual and satellite reasoning can only narrow candidate locations.

great-divergence.reason: Comparability problems (in-kind pay, baskets, occupations) remain unresolved despite extensive prior work. New archival compilation may help modestly.

mesopotamian-chronology.reason: Dendro and radiocarbon work has narrowed the field toward the Middle Chronology. Integrating anchors could yield a defensible answer, but disputes persist.

newton-alchemy-sources.reason: Text-matching unattributed passages against digitized alchemical literature is tractable for an agent team. Repeated formulae complicate attribution, but many passages should resolve.

amazon-cacao.reason: Linking present forest abundance to colonial planting needs field and genetic data. The archive alone gives correlation at best.

sydney-smallpox.reason: Makassan versus First Fleet origins remain contested. The chronological gap probably lacks documents, and the theory carries major political weight.

copernicus-maragha.reason: Decades of searching have produced no transmission document. New digitized Byzantine manuscripts give a small chance of a link.

cocoliztli.reason: Pathogen identification needs aDNA beyond existing published samples. Symptom texts are compatible with several diseases.

rongorongo.reason: The corpus is small and carving dates are uncertain. Testing for post-1770 contact influence is possible, but a convincing verdict is unlikely.

shapira-scrolls.reason: The objects are lost and the transcriptions conflict. Linguistic analysis has recently revived the authenticity case, yet without the leather the question stays contested.

meroitic.reason: The lack of bilinguals is the binding constraint. Computational comparison may extend some lexicon, but full translation is unlikely.

galen-arabic.reason: Matching Hunayn's list against digitized manuscripts and quotations is a strong agent task. Partial identifications of lost works are plausible.

china-1600.reason: Fiscal quotas mask real counts, and wartime survival of records is uneven. The estimate range will stay wide.

beowulf.reason: Linguistic and metrical arguments are already exhaustively debated, and no new evidence class is available.

roman-census.reason: The high/low count dispute rests on interpreting the census jump, and survey evidence is heterogeneous. A decisive answer is unlikely.

medieval-cattle-plagues.reason: A systematic chronicle database with dedup could map spread direction. Ambiguous notices limit certainty.

sloane-informants.reason: Cross-linking catalogues, labels and correspondence can name some enslaved and Indigenous informants. Many will stay unnamed, but partial answers are checkable.

indian-ocean-slave-trade.reason: Records are partial across empires and local carriers left little trace. A convincing total is unlikely, though a database would be valuable.

gutenberg-type.reason: Image analysis can test the hand-mould hypothesis against the Agüera y Arcas/Paul Needham claims, but imaging artifacts confound it. Physical examination would be needed.

ibn-battuta.reason: Borrowed passages can be detected by text reuse, giving strong negative evidence for some legs. Confirming the rest is harder.

padang-1697.reason: The dispatch plus other VOC records may constrain timing. Rupture identification depends on coral and modeling ambiguity.

kerala-jesuits.reason: A smoking-gun letter is unlikely, and much correspondence is undigitized. Absence of evidence will not be convincing.

silent-film-fragments.reason: Matching footage to synopses and the trade press is well suited to agents, and identifications are checkable. Each is small, but they compound.

indigenous-slavery.reason: Euphemism and regional gaps prevent a convincing hemispheric total. Regional estimates are more feasible.

toromiro-provenance.reason: Accession records can trace some lineages. Genetics, which is beyond reach, would be needed for others. The work has conservation value.

leprosy-americas.reason: The parallel Florentine texts and dictionaries are accessible, and a textual analysis answer is very feasible.

hidden-vocabularies.reason: Systematic scanning of digitized books finds checkable lists, and the existing catalogue gives a baseline. This opens evidence for many languages.

ottoman-tahrir.reason: Changes in register type and units confound the trend. Careful reanalysis may clarify but is unlikely to be decisive.

khipu.reason: Few secure khipu–document pairings exist. Pattern analysis may show non-numeric structure, but reading signs is unlikely.

james-pawpaw-remedy.reason: Textual comparison of the recipe and manuscript plus Sloane provenance trails is tractable. The route is the uncertain part. The result would credit an enslaved healer.

early-syphilis.reason: Dated contemporary documents can be sorted from retrospective accounts. A checkable earliest description is plausible.

ternate-gingie.reason: The records concern officials, not growers. Other VOC records might add detail, but the answer is likely to stay thin.

lost-editions.reason: Capture–recapture style estimation is feasible, but format biases make estimates model-dependent. A defensible range is possible.

gregorian-chant.reason: Late notation of Old Roman melodies leaves the stemma underdetermined, and the debate is long-standing.

song-iron.reason: Collection-rate disputes underlie the competing estimates (Hartwell vs critics). Limited archaeology keeps it unresolved.

irish-1641.reason: Deduplicating the depositions is a strong agent task for Protestant deaths. Coverage bias limits a full total.

borneo-elephants.reason: The Sulu–Borneo leg is undocumented, and genetics, which is beyond reach, bears most of the evidential weight.

dunhuang-fragments.reason: Image and text matching across IDP is tractable, and joins are checkable. It enables many manuscript studies.

hittite-fragments.reason: Searchable transcriptions allow systematic join and duplicate detection, which specialists can verify. It feeds edition work.

mendel.reason: The 'too good' statistics are established, but the 'why' lacks working records. The cause will stay speculative.

renaissance-lute.reason: Comparing the Bern partbook with intabulations can test recovery of missing voices. Arranger changes limit fidelity, but many matches are checkable.

gunpowder.reason: The intermediate links are lost, and the route via Mongols or the Islamic world stays inferential.

plague-disappearance.reason: Many causal hypotheses fit uneven data, and records cannot isolate quarantine effects convincingly.

anonymous-serials.reason: Text reuse across digitized newspapers can locate bylines. Propagated errors need care. It could recover many writers.

proto-elamite.reason: Structural analysis suggests some linguistic features, but proving language encoding and descent from short accounting texts is hard.

anonymous-imprints.reason: Damaged type and ornament matching has been proven at scale. Subscription access limits coverage, but checkable attributions are likely and broadly reusable.

archimedes-leaf-170.reason: Key ownership correspondence is offline and the leaf is likely in private hands; locating it refines provenance but adds little text beyond the 1906 photograph.

vermeer.reason: Geometric and optical modeling of high-res paintings can test camera obscura hypotheses, but lacking documentary proof keeps positive attribution contested; an answer would reshape Dutch Golden Age studio history.

zhou-conquest.reason: Combining bronze inscriptions, astronomical retrocalculation, and published radiocarbon dates narrows candidates, though disputed calendar conventions remain a hurdle; a firm year anchors early Chinese chronology and archaeology.

wax-cylinder-voices.reason: Public audio transfers, discographies, and digitized family papers allow acoustic and archival matching to confirm candidates like Grant; adds concrete primary audio and transferable matching methods for sound archives.

yamatai.reason: The Chinese itinerary is geographically contradictory and digitized site reports already support competing Kyushu/Kinai models; resolving it would anchor early Japanese state formation and East Asian diplomacy.

eruption-1809.reason: Checking the 1836 account's Latin source and digitized colonial/Pacific records can resolve the 1808-vs-1818 discrepancy and test candidate volcanoes; pinpoints a major 19th-century climate-forcing event.

oracle-bones.reason: Graph-frequency, contextual, and paleographic analysis across digital corpora can crack some signs, though rare personal/place names resist decipherment; unlocks thousands of Shang divination records.

indus.reason: Short ~5-sign inscriptions and no bilinguals make statistical/computational tests of linguistic syntax inconclusive; resolving it would transform South Asian Bronze Age and writing history.

qing-literacy.reason: Large-scale analysis of digitized contracts can quantify signing vs. marks and model selection bias, though prose literacy remains indirect; revises social and economic baselines for late imperial China.

americas-1492.reason: Post-epidemic tribute counts and uneven regional archaeology leave fundamental data gaps without new fieldwork; a tighter estimate would reshape hemispheric demographic, colonial, and ecological debates.

punt.reason: Intermediate ports confound goods provenance and existing texts/reports have been heavily mined without fieldwork; localizing Punt would clarify Red Sea trade and Egyptian foreign relations.

cassini-cas-a.reason: Cassini's digitized Paris observing journals allow astrometric reconstruction of the 1671 star notes; confirms or rules out a key historical supernova observation.

ptolemy.reason: Quantitative error-structure, precession, and refraction modeling across all ~1,025 stars vs. Hipparchus fragments can strongly test adaptation; clarifies ancient astronomical practice.

segmented-sleep.reason: Corpus-wide search and deduplication of digitized books, diaries, and court records can separate widespread practice from literary tropes; revises pre-industrial daily life and sleep historiography.

thylacine.reason: Digitized Tasmanian newspapers, bounty ledgers, and graded sightings enable Bayesian extinction-date modeling, though sighting reliability remains noisy; refines conservation baselines.

quran-standardization.reason: Stemmatic and paleographic synthesis of digitized early fragments and published radiocarbon dates narrows the window, though parchment-vs-ink gaps persist; central to early Islamic textual history.

justinianic-plague.reason: Digitized papyri, laws, and published pollen/burial studies give indirect, regionally uneven signals without further aDNA/fieldwork; answering it would settle a major late-antique collapse debate.

potato-blight-ships.reason: Cross-referencing digitized port logs, agricultural letters, and newspapers can link candidate Atlantic voyages to early European outbreaks, though farm-level links may stay incomplete.

black-death-africa.reason: Textual coverage is sparse and abandoned settlements lack causal biomarkers without lab work or excavation; a positive or negative answer would reshape global pandemic geography.

silver-china.reason: Unregistered smuggling, uneven route records, and Japanese silver complicate total-volume bounds; tighter estimates would recalibrate early modern global trade and Ming-Qing monetary history.

linear-a.reason: Computational family testing on ~1,500 short texts is feasible, though borrowed Linear B phonetic values add circularity; identifying the family would open Minoan linguistics and Aegean prehistory.

wilkinson-ciphers.reason: Published code-word pairs, digitized dictionaries, and contemporary readings allow computational cryptanalysis of available dispatches, limited mainly by offline originals; clarifies early US-Spanish intrigue.

russian-flu.reason: Digitized London reports and Danish burial records allow age-standardized mortality modeling across waves; clarifies pandemic age shifts and historical coronavirus/influenza hypotheses.

jupiter-red-spot.reason: Dated Paris and Marseille drawings paired with Jovian rotation/ephemeris calculations can test whether early marks match the Great Red Spot; refines planetary atmospheric history.

indian-ocean-tsunamis.reason: Systematic searches of digitized Ming records and regional chronicles can confirm if contemporary scribes noted the c. 1394/1450 waves, though sparse local survival may yield only a qualified negative.

mughal-dodo.reason: Known ship logs and Mundy's account do not link a specific bird to the painter, so resolution depends on finding an overlooked digitized Persian or Dutch record; adds a minor art/trade detail.

agade.reason: Cuneiform itineraries and satellite paleochannels narrow search zones, but without excavation and an in-situ inscription localization remains unverified; anchors Sargonic imperial geography.

great-divergence.reason: Digitized grain prices and company accounts allow better basket standardization, though payment-in-kind and occupational comparability limit certainty; central to global economic history.

mesopotamian-chronology.reason: Integrating king lists, Venus-tablet variants, tree rings, and published radiocarbon dates narrows Low/Middle/High options, though damaged copies leave residual ambiguity; anchors ancient Near Eastern synchronisms.

newton-alchemy-sources.reason: Fuzzy text-reuse and n-gram matching between transcribed Newton notebooks and digitized alchemical corpora can attribute many passages; maps Newton's reading network for science historians.

amazon-cacao.reason: Colonial shipping records cannot prove where wild-harvested vs. planted beans grew without genetic/ecological fieldwork; clarifies Indigenous vs. colonial agroforestry legacies.

sydney-smallpox.reason: Incomplete intervening chronology between Dutch East Indies records and 1789 Sydney accounts leaves transmission routes speculative; bears directly on Australian contact demography.

copernicus-maragha.reason: Comparing digitized Islamic, Byzantine, and European manuscripts with Copernicus's annotations can find closer textual bridges, though an unrecorded oral or lost intermediary may leave transmission open.

cocoliztli.reason: Symptom descriptions are clinically ambiguous and published aDNA covers too few sites/dates; resolving both 1545 and 1576 pathogens without new lab work is unlikely, though high-impact for Mexican demography.

rongorongo.reason: Structural/computational analysis of ~24 digitized inscriptions vs. contact-era scripts can test stimulus-diffusion hypotheses, though wood-vs-carving dating gaps persist; informs world history of writing.

shapira-scrolls.reason: The physical strips are lost, surviving sketches conflict, and key archival papers remain offline; settling authenticity would either add a major biblical witness or close a famous forgery debate.

meroitic.reason: Known phonetic values help, but scarce bilinguals and limited non-funerary texts block full grammatical/lexical translation; unlocking Meroitic would open Kushite history from internal sources.

galen-arabic.reason: Matching Hunayn's bibliographic list against digitized Arabic/Syriac medical corpora and manuscript images can uncover misattributed works; recovers lost ancient medicine and translation history.

china-1600.reason: Ming fiscal quotas diverge from real population and wartime gazetteer survival is uneven, limiting precision; better bounds would reshape Ming-Qing transition and global demography.

beowulf.reason: With only one ~1000 CE manuscript, computational metrical/linguistic dating still struggles to separate original composition from scribal layering; informs Old English literary and cultural history.

roman-census.reason: Textual totals jump fourfold under Augustus and published field surveys use incompatible small-site methodologies; resolving low vs. high counts reshapes Roman economic and military history.

medieval-cattle-plagues.reason: Spatiotemporal mapping and stemmatic deduplication across digitized Latin, Arabic, and Irish chronicles can trace directional spread, despite vague weather/famine conflations; clarifies medieval agrarian crises.

sloane-informants.reason: Cross-linking digitized Sloane catalogues, labels, and correspondence can recover many unnamed or obscured contributors, though composite entries remain tangled; illuminates colonial knowledge extraction.

indian-ocean-slave-trade.reason: Partial digitization of Portuguese/French archives and sparse local-carrier records leave large blind spots; tighter aggregate estimates would reshape Indian Ocean and global slavery historiography.

gutenberg-type.reason: High-res image analysis can quantify glyph variation, but inking, paper impression, and photography confound physical casting mechanics without metallurgical tests; informs early printing technology.

ibn-battuta.reason: Automated text-reuse detection across digitized Arabic corpora can systematically flag borrowed passages, though proving he actually visited unattested stops is harder; calibrates a core 14th-c. source.

padang-1697.reason: Digitized Dutch dispatches and published coral data constrain timing and surge behavior, though uncertain wave heights allow multiple rupture models; refines Sumatran paleoseismology.

kerala-jesuits.reason: Key Jesuit correspondence remains undigitized and mathematical parallels alone do not prove transmission; confirming a link would revise early modern calculus history.

silent-film-fragments.reason: Comparing digitized Eye Filmmuseum footage, copyright synopses, and trade press makes concrete title identifications highly likely; recovers lost films and opens archive collections.

indigenous-slavery.reason: Partly digitized archives, legal euphemisms, and sharp regional gaps prevent a tight hemispheric total; better bounds would transform colonial labor and Indigenous demographic history.

toromiro-provenance.reason: Herbarium vouchers and partly digitized accession/donor records can trace several cultivated lineages, despite some undated specimens; aids botanical conservation and Rapa Nui plant history.

leprosy-americas.reason: The Digital Florentine Codex and Nahuatl dictionaries/texts enable systematic philological analysis of Nahua disease categories vs. Spanish glosses; clarifies colonial medical translation.

hidden-vocabularies.reason: Automated OCR/pattern scanning of digitized travel books and natural histories, deduplicated against the 42-language catalogue, will reliably surface new lists; provides primary data for linguists.

ottoman-tahrir.reason: Changing tax-register units complicate comparisons, but cross-register statistical modeling on digitized/published surveys can test real decline vs. fiscal shift; reshapes 17th-c. Ottoman crisis debates.

khipu.reason: Public databases enable structural clustering, but too few khipus pair securely with colonial translations to crack non-numerical semantics; decipherment would transform Andean historiography.

james-pawpaw-remedy.reason: Comparing the 1736 print recipe against digitized Sloane manuscripts and correspondence can likely trace how the text entered Sloane's collection; offers a case study in colonial medical provenance.

early-syphilis.reason: Systematic corpus auditing of digitized early prints and manuscript catalogues can filter retrospective attributions and pinpoint earliest contemporary notices; informs Columbian Exchange debates.

ternate-gingie.reason: The two digitized Dutch records reflect official edicts rather than growers or enforcement; finding more requires unindexed VOC Ternate papers online; adds a microhistory of early modern drug regulation.

lost-editions.reason: Capture-recapture and survival modeling across early-print catalogues, inventories, and fragments can bound loss rates by format; calibrates survival bias across all book history.

gregorian-chant.reason: Unnotated early Frankish books and centuries-later Old Roman melodies create a structural evidence gap, even with phylogenetic melodic modeling; settles a core medieval musicology debate.

song-iron.reason: Digitized fiscal compilations record receipts, but disputed tax-to-output ratios and limited published archaeology leave wide uncertainty; informs Song proto-industrialization debates.

irish-1641.reason: Deduplicating and network-modeling ~8,000 digitized depositions yields stronger Protestant death bounds, though uneven Catholic coverage limits total-death certainty; improves civil-war historiography.

borneo-elephants.reason: VOC records document elephants in Java, but the proposed Sulu-to-Borneo leg lacks documentary proof and native status hinges on genetics/lab work; clarifies Southeast Asian biogeography.

dunhuang-fragments.reason: Image-matching edges/scripts and text-matching across IDP's dispersed collections can reliably rejoin many fragments despite variable scans; reconstructs Silk Road manuscripts for many fields.

hittite-fragments.reason: Automated text-matching in TLHdig paired with available museum photos can identify many same-text parallels and physical joins; directly advances Hittite textual editions.

mendel.reason: Reanalyzing published counts can test statistical anomalies, but missing working notebooks prevent proving *why* counts are close; clarifies foundational genetics history.

renaissance-lute.reason: Comparing the digitized Bern tenor partbook and catalogues against lute intabulations can match and reconstruct missing vocal lines, accounting for ornamentation; recovers lost Renaissance polyphony.

gunpowder.reason: Terminological and recipe stemmatics across digitized Chinese, Arabic, and Latin texts refine chronologies, though missing intermediate translations may obscure the exact route; key to Eurasian tech transfer.

plague-disappearance.reason: Uneven online port and quarantine records make isolating quarantine vs. ecological or immunity factors difficult without broader data; settles a major debate in European public-health history.

anonymous-serials.reason: Cross-printing byline matching, stylometry, and syndication-error filtering across digitized 19th-century newspapers can attribute many unsigned stories; expands women's literary history.

proto-elamite.reason: Large tablet corpora allow computational sign-distribution comparisons with Linear Elamite, though undeciphered non-numerical signs and lack of bilinguals limit certainty; informs early Iranian writing.

anonymous-imprints.reason: Type-damage and ornament matching across open scanned 18th-century British books can identify many printers, limited mainly by subscription-only archives; enables large-scale bibliographic attribution.

archimedes-leaf-170.reason: Ruling and damage could authenticate the leaf in a newly noticed sale photograph, but tracking it to a present owner requires a later link in the custody record. Locating it would restore access to a witness whose text is already partly recoverable from the photograph.

vermeer.reason: A device can reproduce a painted effect without having caused it. An inventory entry or a pattern of optical effects distinctive to a particular working method would change how historians reconstruct Vermeer’s practice and test other paintings.

zhou-conquest.reason: An inscription and a celestial event could select a year if their readings hold across plausible calendar reconstructions. A secure year would anchor the dynastic transition and let scholars synchronize dated objects and events on either side of it.

wax-cylinder-voices.reason: A dated recording session, a spoken introduction and an independently documented visit could identify some speakers, even where timbre alone is inconclusive. Restoring names would turn anonymous performances into sources for biography, speech and recording history.

yamatai.reason: Settlement scale and the dates of imported goods can eliminate candidates, but several political centres could fit a corrected itinerary. Locating Himiko’s seat would change accounts of early state formation and connect excavated sites with a named polity.

eruption-1809.reason: The conflicting dates deprive the Javanese attribution of its apparent eyewitness support. Independent local accounts would have to match the ice-core timing and distinguish a major eruption from a coincident smaller one. A source would connect climate records with regional histories of the event.

oracle-bones.reason: Recurring divination formulae can constrain particular signs, but a graph attested once in a name may have no recoverable meaning. Reading a large share of the outstanding graphs would transform accounts of Shang society and make previously opaque records usable across the corpus.

indus.reason: Short sequences can exhibit ordering rules under either a linguistic or a non-linguistic interpretation. A diagnostic contrast across contexts would substantially change accounts of early South Asian literacy and determine which kinds of interpretation can be attempted across the seal corpus.

qing-literacy.reason: Contracts can support local estimates if marks and handwriting are assigned to the right people. A population estimate also needs evidence for women, non-signers and reading without writing. Credible bounds would change comparisons of education and permit regional tests of access to print.

americas-1492.reason: Reconstructions can combine tribute districts and dated settlements, but early epidemic losses have to be inferred across vast, unevenly sampled areas. A defensible continental range would alter estimates of demographic collapse and supply regional baselines for environmental and colonial history.

punt.reason: Provenance evidence and sailing logistics can narrow the trading coast, though an animal’s origin need not identify the port Egyptians visited. A convincing regional location would redraw the geography of Red Sea exchange and focus comparisons with local archaeological assemblages.

cassini-cas-a.reason: The decisive find would be a dated position or a chart sufficiently precise to distinguish the transient from a previously uncatalogued star. Such an observation would change the remnant’s historical light record and provide a contemporary constraint for supernova studies.

ptolemy.reason: Epoch-dependent coordinate errors across groups of stars can reveal systematic adaptation even with few surviving Hipparchan observations. Distinguishing inherited positions from fresh ones would revise accounts of ancient observational practice and guide use of the catalogue as evidence.

segmented-sleep.reason: Counting independent nights in diaries or testimony with a known denominator can say more about prevalence than counting mentions of ‘first sleep.’ Silence about ordinary nights limits the estimate. Firm results would change the history of daily routines and enable comparisons across settings.

thylacine.reason: Verified captures anchor survival, but late sightings with no physical record leave extinction intervals sensitive to the observation model. A robust time window would revise the history of the animal’s decline and help assess the reliability of other extinction chronologies.

quran-standardization.reason: Shared spelling peculiarities across early witnesses can date a common written ancestor relative to independently dated copies. Dating the wider adoption of that text is harder. A convincing interval would reshape early Islamic textual history and order work on regional variants.

justinianic-plague.reason: Pathogen-positive burials establish presence more readily than mortality rates. Linking local death estimates to disruption while allowing for war and migration is harder still. A convincing reconstruction would change explanations of late antique transformations and enable regional comparisons of recovery.

potato-blight-ships.reason: A named cargo linked through an importer to a dated outbreak could establish a shipment-level association. Port arrival by itself leaves the farm connection open. Such links would revise the geography of the epidemic’s arrival and give later work documented routes to test.

black-death-africa.reason: A securely dated, diagnostically specific report or published burial finding at one sub-Saharan site could settle presence. Abandonment alone fits several causes. Establishing the plague’s reach would change fourteenth-century African and Indian Ocean histories and guide regional chronology.

silver-china.reason: Overlapping mint, shipment and treasury series constrain flows, but unregistered cargo and Japanese supplies admit different totals. A range robust to both would recalibrate accounts of early global trade and permit stronger comparisons of money supply and prices.

linear-a.reason: Held-out tests can expose chance resemblances, but sign readings and administrative formulae constrain how much evidence a family match supplies. A reproducible linguistic identification would recast Aegean prehistory and open the tablet corpus to sustained interpretation.

wilkinson-ciphers.reason: Edition-specific code–word matches can be tested against contemporary readings before extending them to unread passages. Successful decoding would add direct evidence about Wilkinson’s dealings with Spanish officials and furnish a key for related correspondence.

russian-flu.reason: Age-specific excess deaths against local non-epidemic baselines can be compared across waves without trusting every cause-of-death label. Agreement after harmonizing age bands would identify a shift in mortality risk and supply benchmarks for historical pandemic comparisons.

jupiter-red-spot.reason: Repeated marks with compatible latitude, appearance and rotation on independently dated drawings could establish a sighting in the gap. Single marks are ambiguous. A secure sequence would extend the observational history and help investigate the longevity of Jovian storms.

indian-ocean-tsunamis.reason: Distinctive flooding at the right coast and date in an independent chronicle could verify a contemporary notice. The deposits alone cannot identify an account. Finding one would add human testimony about the disasters and help correlate other coastal evidence.

mughal-dodo.reason: The voyage account and Surat sightings establish opportunities for transfer, but identifying the painter’s subject requires a court, merchant or gift record joining those routes. A provenance would revise the painting’s interpretation and document a route for live animal exchange.

agade.reason: Texts and river courses can rank sites, but channels shifted and relative geography can fit multiple settlements. A secure location would reorder the political geography of the Sargonic empire and anchor archaeological and textual investigations across central Mesopotamia.

great-divergence.reason: Matched occupations, seasons and plausible consumption baskets can show whether wage differences survive alternative assumptions, although Bengal and delta samples may remain narrow. A robust comparison would change the chronology of living-standard divergence and enable tests with other regions.

mesopotamian-chronology.reason: Concordance between tree-ring sequences, dated samples and regnal synchronisms could discriminate among chronologies despite damaged astronomical texts. Fixed absolute dates would revise accounts of political change and anchor comparisons across the interconnected Near East.

newton-alchemy-sources.reason: An unusual wording, error or sequence of recipes reproduced in a particular edition can establish some sources amid much recycled material. Identifications would reconstruct Newton’s reading and let scholars distinguish borrowed procedures from his revisions or experiments.

amazon-cacao.reason: Settlement names and current cacao density do not identify which stands people planted, or when. Direct descriptions of managed groves could support local estimates. A regional fraction would change accounts of colonial forest management and inform studies of surviving landscapes.

sydney-smallpox.reason: Accounts at both ends leave room for multiple transmission routes, and an epidemic elsewhere in the archipelago supplies no intermediate contact. Establishing a chain into Sydney would change explanations of a devastating Aboriginal outbreak and clarify the contact networks behind it.

copernicus-maragha.reason: A dated intermediary manuscript with a traceable reader or annotation could distinguish a route of transmission from independent use of similar devices. Such evidence would revise the intellectual genealogy of European astronomy and connect manuscript traditions for further study.

cocoliztli.reason: A pathogen identified in a burial series may explain one locality without explaining both named epidemics; descriptions also encompass several illnesses. A well-supported attribution across dates would change histories of colonial mortality and permit more specific studies of vulnerability.

rongorongo.reason: A demonstrably linguistic reading and a secure carving chronology relative to outside contact are both difficult to extract from the few surviving objects. Establishing independent invention would change comparative accounts of writing and give researchers a firmer context for reading the tablets.

shapira-scrolls.reason: A shared transcription error tied to a modern exemplar could substantiate forgery even without the strips. Positive authentication from conflicting copies is harder. Resolution would affect either the textual history of Deuteronomy or the history of biblical forgery and inform use of the surviving copies.

meroitic.reason: Parallel passages and inscriptions with independently identifiable events could support checkable translations of some non-funerary texts. Known sound values alone give little semantic control. Success would add Kushite accounts of institutions and put a wider inscription corpus to historical use.

galen-arabic.reason: A translator’s description, a distinctive sequence of arguments and independent quotations can identify an untitled or misattributed witness. Recoveries would alter accounts of Galen’s oeuvre and make new texts available for histories of medicine and translation.

china-1600.reason: Local household series might correct stale fiscal counts, but displacement, omitted households and war losses are hard to separate across regions. Credible estimates for both dates and deaths would revise Ming–Qing demographic history and supply baselines for research on recovery.

beowulf.reason: Meter and sound changes can bound the linguistic ancestry of passages, but successive performance and copying need not leave a single datable composition. A convincing date would change the poem’s political and literary context and sharpen comparisons across Old English verse.

roman-census.reason: Regional settlement trends and demographic accounting could test which definition of citizen makes successive censuses coherent. Neither method directly recovers the counting rule. A defensible population scale would change accounts of Roman expansion and models of manpower and landholding.

medieval-cattle-plagues.reason: Source genealogy and dated independent notices can test the direction of spread; a shared eastward reference in derivative chronicles adds little. Comparable chronologies for all three episodes would change histories of livestock contagion and make trade and weather explanations testable.

sloane-informants.reason: Cross-references among specimens, dates, letters and households can recover some individual suppliers, while other entries merge several contributions. Secure attributions would revise histories of medical authorship and allow researchers to follow informants through collections and correspondence.

indian-ocean-slave-trade.reason: Registers can anchor several colonial routes, but local and inter-island carriage may escape all overlapping records. A defensible range would alter the scale assigned to Indian Ocean enslavement and support comparisons of routes, labour markets and population change.

gutenberg-type.reason: Repeated impressions can isolate stable features of individual sorts from printing noise. Several casting methods may nevertheless generate similar shapes. Identifying a distinctive manufacturing signature would change accounts of early printing and permit comparison across workshops.

ibn-battuta.reason: Borrowing can identify how a passage was written without settling whether the author visited. Independent records and tight chronological contradictions can adjudicate some itineraries. A substantiated reconstruction would change how the Riḥla is used for travel and regional history.

padang-1697.reason: Reports from several places can constrain tsunami simulations, but uncertain surge heights may fit several rupture geometries. A distinctive source would clarify the 1697 event and improve the historical record used to interpret past Sumatran earthquakes.

kerala-jesuits.reason: A missionary copy, translation or letter naming a mathematical result and its recipient could establish a link. Resemblance between series gives little route information. A secure answer would revise histories of mathematical exchange and direct work toward associated correspondence.

silent-film-fragments.reason: Distinctive scene order, intertitles and actors can be checked against contemporary synopses; alternate release titles must be reconciled to establish a new identification. Recoveries restore particular films to cinema history and make footage usable for studies of style, performance and distribution.

indigenous-slavery.reason: Sales and litigation can establish local minima, but evasion under changing legal labels defeats straightforward extrapolation across four centuries. A defensible total range would revise the scale of Indigenous dispossession and permit comparative studies of labour systems and depopulation.

toromiro-provenance.reason: Accession numbers, propagation records and dated beds can trace particular lineages to a documented wild collection. Unrecorded substitutions limit coverage. Confirmed lines would reconstruct the tree’s ex situ history and identify material for comparative or conservation research.

leprosy-americas.reason: Parallel texts can reveal where Nahua writers used a different category from a Spanish gloss, with patient narratives testing dictionary meanings. An account grounded in their own words would revise colonial disease history and inform studies of language, disability and translation.

hidden-vocabularies.reason: Unindexed lists can be verified against the page and checked for dependence on earlier lists through wording and error patterns. Independent attestations would strengthen the historical record of little-documented languages and supply reusable evidence for linguistic and community research.

ottoman-tahrir.reason: Tracking the same settlements across register changes can distinguish some tax reclassification from depopulation. Flight and changing exemptions still complicate headcounts. A robust finding would change accounts of provincial crisis and calibrate uses of Ottoman fiscal records elsewhere.

khipu.reason: Repeated non-numeric patterns in securely paired records could yield readings that predict an unseen person or group. Most cords lack such anchors. A reproducible reading would transform accounts of Andean recordkeeping and open many objects to historical interpretation.

james-pawpaw-remedy.reason: A distinctive textual sequence, shared error or intermediate copy could connect the unnamed recipe to Pawpaw’s printed one despite a missing custody link. An attribution would establish a concrete case of lost medical authorship and help trace related copies and collectors.

early-syphilis.reason: Contemporary dating and comparison of diagnostic detail can distinguish early descriptions of the outbreak from later recollections. Establishing the earliest secure witness would refine the chronology of recognition and anchor work on circulation of medical reports.

ternate-gingie.reason: The proclamation identifies official concerns; a prosecution, deposition or named transaction would be stronger evidence for actual growers and smokers. Identifications would recover local participation in the cannabis trade and guide work on everyday practice under Dutch rule.

lost-editions.reason: Discovery histories and inventories can estimate missing editions among well-observed genres. Formats absent from every sample make the overall estimate sensitive to assumptions. A credible range would revise the scale and mix of print production and help other historians correct survival bias.

gregorian-chant.reason: Shared innovations across regional melodies can indicate relationships, but words-only early books leave the proposed ancestral melody unobserved. Resolving the direction of descent would change accounts of liturgical reform and guide comparative study of regional chant traditions.

song-iron.reason: Local receipts can be compared against recorded rates and dated production evidence, though variation in collection and unregistered output may swamp the estimate. A defensible range would revise assessments of Song industrial capacity and anchor comparisons with other economies.

irish-1641.reason: Named victims, places and dates allow deduplication and identification of credible local minima. Poor coverage of some communities makes a general total harder. A robust range would change accounts of the violence and support local studies of victims and testimony.

borneo-elephants.reason: A documented transfer through Sulu would strengthen the royal-gift account but would not by itself exclude an older island population. An answer integrating early records with published evidence of ancestry would clarify Borneo’s fauna and inform histories of animal movement.

dunhuang-fragments.reason: Continuous handwriting, shared physical defects and complementary edges can establish joins independently of repeated text. Reconstructed manuscripts restore passages and provenance, giving scholars of religion, language and book production witnesses dispersed across collections.

hittite-fragments.reason: Transcription overlap can identify duplicates, while matching script, fracture edges and line spacing can establish physical joins where images exist. Restoring texts would change individual historical readings and yield longer witnesses usable across Hittite studies.

mendel.reason: The fit of published counts can be tested under alternative sampling rules, but several classification and reporting processes can produce similar deviations. Identifying the operative explanation would revise accounts of Mendel’s practice and inform study of other published experimental series.

renaissance-lute.reason: Agreements between surviving vocal parts and independent intabulations can identify faithful arrangements and test recoverable missing lines. Establishing a reading would restore particular polyphonic works and give editors and performers a method applicable to other incomplete sources.

gunpowder.reason: A dated intermediary translation, citation or identifiable traveller could connect textual traditions that their relative dates alone do not join. Establishing the route would revise accounts of Eurasian technical exchange and identify networks for studying other transfers.

plague-disappearance.reason: Comparisons between ports with similar exposure and different controls could test quarantine effects, but exposure, ecology and record survival vary together. A convincing causal account would change interpretations of European demographic recovery and enable comparisons of epidemic prevention.

anonymous-serials.reason: An independently credited first printing, author’s letter or payment entry can validate a byline found through reprints. Recovering authors would change accounts of women’s newspaper work and make previously anonymous bodies of fiction available for literary and labour history.

proto-elamite.reason: Accounting structure can explain repeated sign sequences without assigning spoken words, and proposed links to later signs need independent controls. Resolving both questions would alter the early history of writing in Iran and guide interpretation of a substantial archive.

anonymous-imprints.reason: Combinations of damaged ornaments and type can link anonymous books to dated signed editions, especially when chronology controls for material changing hands. New assignments would expose the production of clandestine and commercial print and enable study of printers’ wider output.

archimedes-leaf-170.reason: The photograph could authenticate a rediscovered leaf, but the public ownership trail has breaks and a last recorded owner need not be the present one. Locating it would reunite evidence about the codex and allow fresh comparison with the old photograph.

vermeer.reason: Focus and perspective can be compared across canvases, but several working methods could produce the same effects. Establishing actual use would change accounts of Vermeer's practice and give studies of other painters a documented comparison.

zhou-conquest.reason: Agreement across dated astronomical phenomena and inscriptional sequences could isolate a year, although the matches depend on how the calendar is reconstructed. A secure anchor would link the dynastic transition to excavated assemblages and other early Chinese events.

wax-cylinder-voices.reason: A spoken introduction, a recording itinerary and an independently dated letter could identify a speaker even where timbre is inconclusive. Secure names would restore the circumstances of particular recordings and make related voices and sessions easier to trace.

yamatai.reason: Travel times and archaeological concentrations constrain plausible regions, but neither a wealthy settlement nor a repaired itinerary uniquely identifies Himiko's seat. A secure location would reshape accounts of political consolidation and direct comparisons among contemporary sites.

eruption-1809.reason: The conflict between the printed Java dates undermines a proposed source, and the ice signal by itself identifies no volcano. A secure source would connect a local eruption with global atmospheric change and anchor work on contemporary climate and harvests.

oracle-bones.reason: Repeated contexts can constrain the meanings of some graphs, but thousands include singletons and possible names with no independent gloss. Reading them at the scale asked would transform accounts of Shang institutions and make a large inscriptional archive newly usable.

indus.reason: Short, recurrent seals give little leverage for distinguishing language from an ordered inventory of emblems. Determining what the signs encode would change interpretations of Indus institutions and establish the basis for appropriate comparisons across sites.

qing-literacy.reason: Contracts could establish differences in signing by locality or occupation. Extending them to readers outside property transactions requires assumptions about both selection and skill. A defensible population range would anchor studies of schooling, publishing and social mobility.

americas-1492.reason: In regions first counted after epidemics, different starting populations and loss rates can yield the same surviving figures. An independently defensible continental range would revise the scale of conquest-era loss and provide baselines for regional demographic and land-use studies.

punt.reason: Repeated combinations of products and Egyptian itineraries may delimit a trading region, but an animal's place of origin can lie far from its port of sale. A secure placement would clarify Red Sea exchange and connect expedition records to African sites.

cassini-cas-a.reason: The dated journals present a bounded search, and a sufficiently precise sketch or position could distinguish the object from field stars. The identification would settle a point about Cassini's observing and add an early constraint on the remnant's history.

ptolemy.reason: Systematic offsets and distinctive errors shared with surviving Hipparchan material can identify derivation for portions of the catalogue, even if authorship varies by entry. A credible division would revise accounts of Ptolemy's observing and recover evidence for earlier cataloguing.

segmented-sleep.reason: Runs of dated diaries and depositions provide a denominator in some settings, although authors seldom recorded an ordinary uninterrupted night. A bounded prevalence estimate would distinguish local habits from general claims about preindustrial sleep and supply comparisons across households.

thylacine.reason: Grading independent sightings can narrow the period, but sparse observations near extinction leave the last wild deaths weakly dated. A secure interval would clarify survival after documented captivity and help test retrospective extinction estimates.

quran-standardization.reason: Shared consonantal peculiarities can link early witnesses to an exemplar, with script and material dates placing bounds on its circulation. Establishing when a common text prevailed would revise early Islamic textual history and date the divergence of manuscript traditions.

justinianic-plague.reason: Pathogen-positive burials identify episodes, but the available series seldom measure deaths and social change in the same representative populations. A credible combined answer would change explanations of late antique transformation and calibrate regional studies of epidemics and recovery.

potato-blight-ships.reason: Arrival notices and growers' letters might independently connect a cargo with a named early outbreak, though an infected shipment is hard to infer from timing alone. Verified links would qualify accounts of introduction and support comparisons of commercial and disease routes.

black-death-africa.reason: Dated accounts might identify a localized episode, but abandonment has many causes and sparse sampled burials offer little basis for continent-wide exclusion. Establishing even one securely dated occurrence would change the geography of the pandemic and help reinterpret specific African settlement sequences.

silver-china.reason: Route-by-route reconciliation could yield informative bounds if independent receipts constrain leakage and origin. A convincing estimate would change the measured role of China in early modern bullion flows and supply a basis for comparing monetary shocks across markets.

linear-a.reason: Blinded tests on held-out texts could disfavor chance matches, but borrowed sound values and repetitive accounts allow many language models to fit. A secure identification would transform Aegean language history and let scholars reread an entire administrative corpus.

wilkinson-ciphers.reason: Known readings can test which dictionary edition supplies a code and validate a key on independent letters. Decoding the remaining accessible dispatches would specify what Wilkinson told Spanish officials and support further searches for letters using the same system.

russian-flu.reason: Age-specific all-cause mortality can be compared with seasonal baselines across successive waves within the same reporting system, then checked against the second population. An age shift or convincing stability would refine the epidemic's history and give comparative pandemic studies a reusable series.

jupiter-red-spot.reason: Orientation, predicted visibility and motion across consecutive drawings can distinguish persistent features, though isolated dark marks admit several identifications. A reliable sighting would revise the spot's observational chronology and extend the baseline for studies of its persistence.

indian-ocean-tsunamis.reason: A geographically specific notice of sudden inundation could match a deposit independently, but approximate dates and silence in court records leave either event unresolved. A match would recover contemporary experience of the disasters and calibrate other coastal chronologies.

mughal-dodo.reason: The two records establish the trade and the presence of live birds, while the particular transfer to artist or patron calls for an additional link. Tracing it would explain a cross-cultural natural-history image and connect shipping evidence with Mughal court collecting.

agade.reason: Textual neighbors and reconstructed waterways can narrow the search, but several sites can occupy the same relative position across changing channels. A secure identification would fix the imperial capital in the landscape and give many texts and survey finds a common reference.

great-divergence.reason: Price series and accounts allow explicit household baskets and comparisons within like occupations, but regional conclusions are vulnerable to missing payments and thin wage coverage. Defensible differences or parity would bear directly on the Great Divergence and enable comparison across other labor markets.

mesopotamian-chronology.reason: Independent tree-ring, radiocarbon and textual constraints can exclude rival chronologies where their anchors genuinely coincide. A secure absolute sequence would date events across interacting kingdoms and provide a framework for many excavation and exchange chronologies.

newton-alchemy-sources.reason: Long verbal matches, shared errors and matching sequences of extracts can distinguish specific texts from common recipes for some passages. Identifications would document Newton's reading choices and recover source relationships useful in other early modern notebooks.

amazon-cacao.reason: Village exports and modern forest abundance do not date local trees or identify where exported cacao grew. Establishing the colonial share would alter interpretations of Amazonian forest history and furnish a baseline for studies of other managed species.

sydney-smallpox.reason: Contemporary reports at either end leave considerable room for different chains of transmission into Sydney. Identifying one would change interpretations of an early colonial disaster and help reconstruct Indigenous and maritime connections before the outbreak.

copernicus-maragha.reason: A dated intermediary with distinctive notation and a demonstrable connection to Copernicus could establish a route, but parallel constructions alone leave it open. An answer would change the genealogy of early modern astronomy and identify manuscripts or networks relevant to other transfers.

cocoliztli.reason: Pathogen evidence from one cemetery cannot readily be extended to both waves, and overlapping symptoms permit multiple causes. A convincing attribution would revise explanations of demographic catastrophe in New Spain and guide interpretation of other epidemic accounts and burials.

rongorongo.reason: Even a securely dated piece of wood does not establish when its signs were carved or whether they encoded speech. A convincing result would affect comparative accounts of writing's origins and give the corpus a firmer context for analysis.

shapira-scrolls.reason: Variant sketches and accounts could expose a specific modern source for a reading, but with the strips missing many material tests cannot be replicated. A verdict would settle a consequential disputed biblical witness and clarify the evidentiary standing of its transcriptions.

meroitic.reason: Known sound values and parallel contexts make independently testable readings of some new passages credible, although free translation faces a shortage of bilingual controls. Such gains would recover Kushite testimony beyond epitaphs and give later researchers vocabulary and grammatical checks.

galen-arabic.reason: Distinctive quotations and the translator's descriptions can corroborate the identity of a manuscript even when its title has changed. Recovering lost Galenic material would revise the history of ancient medicine and supply texts for translation, editing and reception studies.

china-1600.reason: Gazetteers can expose stale quotas, but missing wartime households may have fled or fallen outside registration, leaving actual deaths particularly uncertain. Defensible estimates would change accounts of the Ming-Qing transition and support regional comparisons of war and recovery.

beowulf.reason: Metrical and linguistic features constrain periods, but oral transmission, scribal modernization and a single late witness make a narrow composition date difficult. Secure dating would relocate the poem in English political and literary history and anchor comparisons with other verse.

roman-census.reason: Settlement trajectories can check the plausibility of rival readings of the census, but site counts map imperfectly onto people with citizen status. A defensible total would reshape explanations of Augustan enfranchisement and furnish a denominator for Roman military and social history.

medieval-cattle-plagues.reason: Independent dated notices can test the direction of spread, although gaps to the east and ambiguous accounts of animal mortality complicate conclusions for all three plagues. Establishing their routes would clarify livestock exchange and offer a chronology for later epizootic comparisons.

sloane-informants.reason: A label and letter can sometimes trace a distinct piece of knowledge past the named intermediary, though composite entries limit generalization. Identifying particular suppliers would redistribute credit in medical collecting and connect catalogue entries to otherwise dispersed personal histories.

indian-ocean-slave-trade.reason: Deduplicating transfers and voyages can establish substantial minima, but poorly observed local routes leave wide uncertainty in aggregate totals. A convincing estimate would revise the scale and geography of coerced migration and enable comparisons with other slave trades.

gutenberg-type.reason: Recurring details across impressions could distinguish recurring matrices from transient ink effects, yet different casting techniques may leave equivalent printed traces. Resolving the process would refine the history of early typography and give investigators a diagnostic for other workshops.

ibn-battuta.reason: Borrowed prose can establish literary dependence, while a traveller could still have visited the place described. Securely establishing which journeys occurred would change use of the narrative as historical testimony and distinguish firsthand evidence for several regions.

padang-1697.reason: The relative timing and distribution of reported surges could rule out some ruptures, but uncertain water heights and ambiguous coral records may leave several candidates. Identification would fix a regional disaster in the historical record and extend the earthquake sequence used in hazard studies.

kerala-jesuits.reason: A letter naming a text, method and recipient might bridge the traditions, but mathematical priority and missionary contact establish only opportunity. Resolving transmission would change accounts of early calculus and clarify which teaching and translation networks merit study.

silent-film-fragments.reason: A distinctive scene sequence can be checked against contemporary synopses, cast photographs and alternate catalogue titles. Identifications would restore works to particular filmographies and make previously anonymous footage available to numerous studies of performance and production.

indigenous-slavery.reason: Sales and suits provide local minima, but concealed enslavement and repeated sales of the same person create errors in opposite directions across four centuries. A defensible overall range would revise accounts of colonial labor and enable regional demographic comparisons.

toromiro-provenance.reason: A voucher, bed location and accession trail can identify descendants where transfers and propagation are documented, though gaps threaten more distant pedigrees. Establishing which stocks have wild provenance would recover collecting histories and inform conservation and botanical comparisons.

leprosy-americas.reason: Parallel passages allow comparison of named conditions, observable symptoms and treatment in their own textual contexts, with other Nahua uses checking translation choices. An answer would recover distinctions obscured by a Spanish disease label and aid studies of colonial description and diagnosis.

hidden-vocabularies.reason: Page-level searching and comparison of list order and errors can uncover independent vocabularies omitted from existing catalogues. Recoveries would document early encounters and supply primary linguistic evidence for historical linguists and the communities concerned.

ottoman-tahrir.reason: Tracking the same settlements across register changes can distinguish some fiscal relabeling from actual loss, though migration and exemptions complicate regional inference. A credible demographic trend would revise accounts of Ottoman crisis and anchor comparisons of settlement and taxation.

khipu.reason: Associations between cord features and named categories might be verified across a few independently documented examples, but scarce secure pairs constrain a reproducible reading. Reading non-numerical signs would revise accounts of Andean recordkeeping and unlock a dispersed primary archive.

james-pawpaw-remedy.reason: Distinctive shared phrasing could establish descent from Pawpaw's recipe if competing printed versions and manuscript dates can be excluded. Demonstrating anonymous transmission would clarify credit for the remedy and give researchers a traceable example of how Sloane acquired medical knowledge.

early-syphilis.reason: Dating the witness and the events it actually describes can distinguish contemporary outbreak accounts from later recollections, though early terminology is ambiguous. Establishing the earliest secure description would refine the European chronology and supply a point of comparison for other putative cases.

ternate-gingie.reason: The proclamation dates official concern, but growers and smokers would need to surface in independent testimony or enforcement records. Identifying them would recover the social setting of cannabis use on Ternate and connect colonial regulation with local trade and practice.

lost-editions.reason: Successive catalogues and inventories permit estimates stratified by format, but editions with almost no chance of leaving evidence dominate the uncertain tail. A defensible range would change estimates of print output and allow survival corrections in studies of readership and genres.

gregorian-chant.reason: Aligning melodies can show relationships, yet missing early notation makes the direction of descent hard to distinguish from shared inheritance. Resolving it would alter accounts of liturgical transmission and give related chant repertories a better historical reference.

song-iron.reason: Local receipts can constrain output where levy rules are independently known, but alternative collection rates substantially change the extrapolated total. An answer would revise the scale of Song industry and anchor studies of its labor, fuel and transport requirements.

irish-1641.reason: Place, time and named victims allow many duplicate reports to be recognized, though sparse coverage of some communities complicates upper bounds. A defensible death toll would recalibrate accounts of the rising and provide a local framework for studying displacement and commemoration.

borneo-elephants.reason: Court elephants in Java establish one link at most, and even a documented gift would require evidence that its descendants account for the Borneo population. Resolving origin would clarify royal animal transfers and inform comparisons of island conservation histories.

dunhuang-fragments.reason: Complementary torn edges, fiber patterns, handwriting and continuous text can corroborate physical joins across collections. Confirmed joins restore manuscripts and their original settings, giving many linguistic, religious and material studies more complete witnesses.

hittite-fragments.reason: Distinctive matching passages can identify parallel copies, and images of compatible breaks and layout can test physical joins in the photographed subset. Recovering texts and tablet groupings would expand the usable Hittite corpus for philology and historical reconstruction.

mendel.reason: Statistical agreement can be quantified under explicit stopping and classification rules, but several such rules could produce the published pattern. Explaining it would change accounts of Mendel's experimental practice and improve the basis for analyzing other historical datasets.

renaissance-lute.reason: A surviving vocal part can check how faithfully particular arrangers transferred lines, making recovery persuasive where several witnesses agree. Identifications would restore details of specific songs and give editors and performers material for further reconstructions.

gunpowder.reason: Chronologically ordered texts constrain possible transmission routes, but actual carriers and intermediate witnesses are hard to document. A demonstrated route would change accounts of Eurasian technical exchange and give related translations and contacts a clearer chronology.

plague-disappearance.reason: Cross-port contrasts and policy changes can test quarantine effects, but simultaneous changes in trade, exposure and ecology leave broad causal attribution uncertain. A convincing explanation would change accounts of European mortality decline and sharpen comparative histories of epidemic control.

anonymous-serials.reason: A reprint under a woman's name can be checked against correspondence, payment records or an independently credited collection to avoid circular attribution. Restoring authorship would change some writers' bibliographies and open unsigned newspaper fiction to broader literary and network studies.

proto-elamite.reason: Administrative recurrence permits structural comparison, yet neither linguistic encoding nor descent follows from shared shapes or accounting conventions. Establishing both relationships would place early Iranian writing in a firmer history and guide interpretation of a large tablet corpus.

anonymous-imprints.reason: Distinctive combinations of damaged ornaments and type in securely dated signed books can identify workshops, with repeated matches helping to track transferred stock. Credible attributions would revise accounts of clandestine and ordinary printing and connect dispersed editions to printers and networks.
